stage_a.note: Both founders smile frequently and maintain a highly positive, upbeat tone throughout the pitch.
Lisa speaks with animated gestures and clear excitement when describing the possibilities of the shoes.
Lisa warmly introduces her husband and daughters, establishing a friendly connection with the panel.

venture.description: Interchangeable kids' shoes with attachable baubles to extend the life and style of the footwear.

turns.speaker: F2
turns.summary: Lisa introduces herself to the panel and begins the presentation of their kids shoe company.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Duc introduces himself and states they are from Huntington Beach, California.

turns.speaker: F2
turns.summary: Lisa explains the common problem parents face when kids rapidly outgrow their shoes.

turns.speaker: S2
turns.summary: Lori agrees, noting that kids outgrow their shoes very quickly.

turns.speaker: F2
turns.summary: Lisa introduces their idea of inventing a single shoe that can be styled for any outfit.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Duc confirms that they successfully created exactly that product.

turns.speaker: F2
turns.summary: Lisa formally introduces Baubles and Soles, their patent-pending interchangeable shoe line.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Duc shows how the shoes can be customized with different baubles for playdates.

turns.speaker: F2
turns.summary: Lisa shows another customization option, demonstrating the versatility of the shoes for parties.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Duc highlights that the shoes are functional, fashionable, machine washable, and slip-resistant.

turns.speaker: F2
turns.summary: Lisa concludes the prepared pitch by asking which shark is ready to partner with them.

turns.speaker: S5
turns.summary: Mark laughs and enthusiastically repeats Lisa's closing remark.

turns.speaker: F2
turns.summary: Lisa introduces their daughter and her friend who will help hand out samples to the panel.

turns.speaker: S4
turns.summary: Robert gives Kaia a high five as she hands him a sample box.

turns.speaker: S5
turns.summary: Mark cheers and encourages the kids as they distribute the shoes.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Duc thanks Audrey for doing a good job handing out the samples.

turns.speaker: S3
turns.summary: Kevin remarks that the kids are very cute.

turns.speaker: F2
turns.summary: Lisa tells the panel that Duc will demonstrate how to attach the baubles to the shoes.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Duc explains the process of supporting the shoe from the inside and twisting the bauble clockwise.

turns.speaker: S5
turns.summary: Mark successfully attaches a bauble and shows it to the rest of the panel.

turns.speaker: F2
turns.summary: Lisa explains that removing the bauble requires pushing it down and twisting counter-clockwise.

turns.speaker: S2
turns.summary: Lori tests the mechanism and confirms that it is very easy to use.

turns.speaker: F2
turns.summary: Lisa says goodbye to the kids as they walk off the set.

turns.speaker: S4
turns.summary: Robert asks the founders how they originally came up with the idea for the business.

turns.speaker: F2
turns.summary: Lisa explains the idea originated from receiving shoes for her daughter that she quickly outgrew.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Duc adds that they obsessed over the idea, studied, and eventually found a mold maker.

turns.speaker: S2
turns.summary: Lori asks how many different attachable bauble designs they currently offer.

turns.speaker: F2
turns.summary: Lisa answers that they currently have about twenty different designs available.

turns.speaker: S5
turns.summary: Mark asks for the cost to manufacture one package of the base shoes.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Duc states the base shoes cost eleven dollars to make, retailing for fifty and wholesaling for twenty-five.

turns.speaker: S2
turns.summary: Lori asks for the retail price of the individual character bauble packages.

turns.speaker: F2
turns.summary: Lisa answers that the baubles cost between thirteen and seventeen dollars depending on the design.

turns.speaker: S2
turns.summary: Lori asks both founders to share their personal and professional backgrounds.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Duc explains he was born in Montreal, earned a film degree, and started a video production company.

turns.speaker: S2
turns.summary: Lori asks Lisa to share her background.

turns.speaker: F2
turns.summary: Lisa shares her journey from a Vietnamese refugee camp to working in banking and non-profits.

turns.speaker: S1
turns.summary: Daymond expresses admiration, noting he has never heard a pitch from someone who lived in a refugee camp.

turns.speaker: S5
turns.summary: Mark points out that her background proves she will be an extremely hard worker.

turns.speaker: F2
turns.summary: Lisa playfully agrees, stating that immigrants get the job done.

turns.speaker: S4
turns.summary: Robert asks the founders for their total sales figures.

turns.speaker: F2
turns.summary: Lisa states they have generated one hundred and fifty thousand dollars in sales over the last twelve months.

turns.speaker: S4
turns.summary: Robert asks what sales channels they used to achieve those figures.

turns.speaker: F2
turns.summary: Lisa explains that eighty percent of their business is currently generated through wholesale and international distribution.

turns.speaker: S4
turns.summary: Robert asks to confirm that eighty percent of their sales are indeed wholesale.

turns.speaker: F2
turns.summary: Lisa confirms the wholesale figure and adds they project three hundred thousand in sales this year.

turns.speaker: S5
turns.summary: Mark asks the founders what they are looking for from a partnership with a shark.

turns.speaker: F2
turns.summary: Lisa states they are looking for a strategic partner to help capture the American market.

turns.speaker: S1
turns.summary: Daymond exits, explaining that the business presents an inventory nightmare with too many sizes and colors.

turns.speaker: F2
turns.summary: Lisa begins to respond to Daymond's concerns regarding the inventory challenges.

turns.speaker: S4
turns.summary: Robert interrupts to emphasize how much he respects Lisa's life story and background.

turns.speaker: F2
turns.summary: Lisa addresses the inventory concern, explaining their process only requires making three hundred pairs at a time.

turns.speaker: S4
turns.summary: Robert exits, stating he doesn't love the product and wouldn't know how to market it.

turns.speaker: F2
turns.summary: Lisa responds to Robert, pointing out that they have done absolutely no advertising so far.

turns.speaker: S5
turns.summary: Mark points out that their lack of advertising is exactly the challenge they face.

turns.speaker: F2
turns.summary: Lisa explains their strategy is to adopt a Build-A-Bear model allowing online customization.

turns.speaker: S5
turns.summary: Mark exits, explaining they are looking for accelerants rather than figuring out how to market their product.

turns.speaker: F2
turns.summary: Lisa politely thanks Mark for his feedback.

turns.speaker: S3
turns.summary: Kevin compliments the founders for coming in with a realistic valuation of six hundred thousand dollars.

turns.speaker: F2
turns.summary: Lisa emphasizes they are there for a deal and have turned down other investments.

turns.speaker: S5
turns.summary: Mark acknowledges her dedication and praises their presentation as remarkable.

turns.speaker: S3
turns.summary: Kevin exits, concluding that despite the good valuation, he does not want to be in the shoe business.

turns.speaker: F2
turns.summary: Lisa appeals to Lori, highlighting that their returning customer rate is an impressive forty-six percent.

turns.speaker: S2
turns.summary: Lori tells Lisa she was deeply moved by her life story and the hardships she overcame.

turns.speaker: S2
turns.summary: Lori exits, explaining that the shoe business is incredibly difficult and competitive.

turns.speaker: F2
turns.summary: Lisa refuses to give up, asking the panel if there is a way they can de-risk the deal.

turns.speaker: S3
turns.summary: Kevin asks Lisa how exactly she proposes to de-risk the investment.

turns.speaker: F2
turns.summary: Lisa suggests paying the investor back their hundred thousand dollars within two years from revenue.

turns.speaker: F2
turns.summary: Lisa passionately appeals to Daymond, expressing absolute confidence that her company will succeed.

turns.speaker: F2
turns.summary: Lisa repeats her offer to Daymond, promising to pay back the investment in two years.

turns.speaker: S1
turns.summary: Daymond expresses doubt that the business is currently at a stage to generate that return.

turns.speaker: F2
turns.summary: Lisa continues to plead with Daymond, reiterating that they came specifically to partner with him.

turns.speaker: S1
turns.summary: Daymond makes an offer of one hundred thousand dollars for twenty-five percent equity.

turns.speaker: F2
turns.summary: Lisa immediately accepts Daymond's offer.

turns.speaker: S1
turns.summary: Daymond hugs the founders and congratulates them on securing a deal.

decisions.note: Inventory nightmare with too many sizes, colors, and accessories to stock.
Does not love the product and wouldn't know how to market it given low direct-to-consumer sales.
Founders are searching for accelerants instead of figuring out how to market the core product.
Does not want to be in the shoe business.
Shoe business is too competitive and difficult.
Decides to make an offer after the founder's persistent appeals and offer to de-risk.
